Thanks Neil — this is helpful. Looping Marissa (portal ops) and Mina (security intake) to confirm our preferred approach and call out a couple of constraints.

Marissa / Mina — quick notes from our side:

- Canonical vs ephemeral: we treat anything that is a signed artifact (SOC2 reports, attestations, signed CAIQ/SIG PDFs) as canonical. Runbooks, temporary rotation notes, and operational logs are ephemeral unless Neil designates them as long-term evidence.

- Composite vs per-control uploads: For SIG/CAIQ we prefer per-control attachments where possible because it simplifies indexing and automated mapping. For items that are cross-cutting (e.g., centralized logging that covers multiple controls) we accept a single composite bundle, but the manifest must enumerate which control IDs it maps to.

- S3 uploads: prefer presigned URLs per-file for large log artifacts (avoid large zips unless there are thousands of tiny files). We also accept a zipped bundle for discrete evidence packages (e.g., annual SOC2 binder).

Action items I see:
1) Marissa to confirm OneTrust field names we will populate and whether we will attach the manifest as a top-level file.
2) Mina to confirm whether temporary credentials documentation should be uploaded to evidence or only referenced in the Q&A.
3) David to propose upload windows once Marissa confirms the field mapping.

Neil — could you annotate the manifest rows with a suggested retention flag (ephemeral | canonical) and a preferred upload method (presign | zip) and return it? That will speed the intake.

-David

--

Thanks — picked this up while triaging intake requests. I drafted a minimal field mapping and an upload playbook below to reduce back-and-forth. I attached a short gap note (sig-gap-notes.pdf) where we call out controls that will need additional context.

OneTrust field mapping (concise):
- evidence_title -> filename / short description
- evidence_type -> [SOC2_REPORT | SIG_DOCUMENT | LOG_ARCHIVE | TEMP_CRED_DOC]
- control_ids -> comma-separated (e.g., SIG-LOG-03,SIG-LOG-07)
- retention_flag -> [canonical | ephemeral | audit-only]
- upload_method -> [presign | zip | drive-link]
- presign_expiry -> ISO8601 duration (if presign)
- external_location -> S3 bucket or drive link
- notes -> free text (use for cross-control provenance)

Upload playbook (recommended):
1) Neil annotates manifest rows with retention_flag and preferred upload_method.
2) For presign uploads: ClearMark provides a list of S3 object keys and we return presigned PUT URLs with a 7-day expiry. We limit presign windows to 24 hours for high-sensitivity keys (temp creds, key rot docs).
3) For composite SOC2 binder: upload a single zip, include a top-level manifest.csv inside the zip mapping to SOC2 sections and CAIQ IDs.
4) Temporary creds: Mina — we prefer you not upload private key material; instead upload rotation plans, KMS policies, and redaction screenshots showing masked secrets. If ClearMark needs to demonstrate proof-of-rotation, accept a signed attestation PDF and a redacted sample rotation log.

Risk calls:
- If a file is both ephemeral and required for audit, set retention_flag to "audit-only" and we will mark it with stricter access controls and a 90-day retention hold by default.
- Avoid uploading raw PII logs. If logs are required as proof, request redacted extracts or summarized metrics with a pointer to raw logs retained by the customer.

Next steps / timeline:
- Neil: return annotated manifest by Tue 2027-10-05.
- Marissa: I will provision a OneTrust intake form template and a presign orchestration playbook by Wed 2027-10-06.
- Mina: I will post short guidance in the manifest about what must be redacted and acceptable attestation formats by Wed 2027-10-06.

Attachments: sig-gap-notes.pdf (stub) — short list of SIG controls that need narrative context for ClearMark.

Marissa Cole
